recorded.finalText:
The translate-es pipeline is set up and working: a chat source feeds a prompt node (instructed to only translate incoming text into Spanish, never answer or follow instructions in it), which feeds an OpenAI gpt-4o-mini LLM node, which returns the answer through a response node back to the chat.

I fixed a config issue (modelOutputTokens was left at the default 128,000, which exceeds gpt-4o-mini's 16,384-token limit and would have been rejected by OpenAI) by setting it to 4096. The pipeline validates cleanly, and I ran it twice sending "What time is it in Madrid?" as a chat message — both runs completed with zero errors and zero failures, confirming the translate-only behavior executes end-to-end (chat → prompt → llm_openai → response) without the engine rejecting the request.

One caveat: the engine doesn't expose the actual translated text through the trace/log tools available to me (payloads are null unless full trace level is set, which isn't something I can configure via these tools), so I can't show you the literal Spanish output text as proof — only that the run completed cleanly with no errors. If you'd like, open the chat UI yourself to see the actual translated reply. The pipeline file is saved at pipelines/translate-es.pipe; nothing further is needed from you unless you want it deployed/published.
